summary: rservices module is minimal — pure presence detection for 512/rexec, 513/rlogin, 514/rsh (bare TCP connect confirmation). One finding kind (r_<svc>) at T0/T1, generic 'high — cleartext, IP-trust auth' with no attempt to send a client packet, capture the login banner, or try a passwordless login as root/bin/daemon (the canonical .rhosts trust names). Biggest gap: the entire attack surface is untouched — no rsh 'echo test' probe against common trust names, no rexec bogus-cred send to capture the auth-failure text (which itself can enumerate valid users), no cleartext_creds recording.

findings.tier_evidence: TCP connect to 512/513/514 succeeded — enum + posture combined; the mere reachability of a Berkeley r-service in 2025 IS the finding, but no protocol handshake or trust-file probe was actually attempted.
findings.promotion_notes: Add a client-packet layer: for rsh 514, speak the protocol (stderr port, null, luser, ruser, cmd all NUL-terminated) with luser=root/ruser=root cmd='id' and read the reply — a shell response means .rhosts trust is open. For rlogin 513, similar handshake with common trust names. Landing any = T3 unauthenticated shell.
findings.tester_next_step: rsh -l root IP id ; rlogin -l root IP ; echo id | rexec -l root -p '' IP ; also try daemon, bin, sync, adm, halt, uucp as trust names; capture -A 'port 512-514' for cleartext-cred proof.
